newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Apr jet/gas oil regrade widens.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Apr jet/gas oil regrade widens.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel/gas oil regrade widened sharply at midday on Wednesday amid poor demand for jet fuel against a strong gas oil market which is still receiving good support for prompt cargoes, traders said.
"The jet fuel market is taking a beating because there is no demand out there," one trader said.

April regrade was last quoted at -80/-55 cents from Tuesday's -60/-40 cents, brokers said. They said the market traded to a low of -65 cents late last night with deals also seen at -55 cents, -50 cents and -48 cents.
In the physical market, late Tuesday, jet fuel was offered down to a low of $25.30 per barrel free-on-board Singapore for a 100,000-barrel cargo loading April 25-30.
Traditionally, jet fuel value slips below gas oil in the second quarter as demand reaches a low as jet-kerosene is no longer needed as a winter heating fuel.
Traders said the sharply lower regrade numbers is also due to sustained support for prompt gas oil in the physical market which is keeping gas oil swaps also firm.
April gas oil was last quoted at $26.45/$26.65 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $26.30/$26.40, brokers said.
The higher prices, they said, was due to buying interest from local trader Hin Leong for prompt gas oil which was bid at $27.20 per barrel fob.
